title: add CI artifact signing, SBOM generation and release provenance manifests for private-installer
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Add cosign artifact signing and Syft-generated SBOMs to private-installer CI; generate per-release provenance and release-manifests to be consumed by the operator and on-prem install pipelines. Backwards compatible with existing release tooling.
description:
Motivation: secure the private-installer release pipeline for on-prem/VPC customers by producing signed artifacts, verifiable SBOMs, and a machine-readable release provenance manifest. This enables customers to validate artifacts in air-gapped environments and meet compliance requirements (CIS/SOC).

Changes included: - Add Cosign signing step to CI for all release artifacts (helm charts, installer bundles, container images). - Generate SBOMs via Syft for each artifact and attach to release artifacts. - Produce release-provenance manifests (JSON) that list artifacts, checksums, signatures, SBOM URLs, and build metadata. - Update release scripts to publish artifacts to the internal release bucket and produce a signed release-manifests tarball. - Add Helm Chart metadata updates (Chart.yaml annotations for provenance) and a lightweight manifest consumer script used by the installer to verify artifacts at install/upgrade time.

Checklist: - [x] CI pipeline steps for build -> sbom -> sign -> publish implemented - [x] Syft SBOM generation configured for container and OPA bundles - [x] Cosign key usage documented (KMS/HSM path and offline signing) - [x] Release-provenance manifest schema defined and emitted - [x] Integration test: release pipeline run on staging produces signed artifacts and a signed release-manifests.tgz - [x] Rollback: installer will skip signed verification if "--no-verify" is passed for fast rollback during incidents

Testing and verification: Ran full staging release (staging bucket) which produced: signed container images (cosign digest signatures), syft SBOMs (spdx-json), and a release-manifests.json that enumerates artifacts and signatures. A separate verification job uses cosign and local KMS credentials to validate signatures and fails-fast on mismatch. CI had one transient flake on the cosign upload step which was retried by the pipeline; final run is green.

Migration and rollout notes: Changes are backwards compatible for existing installs. The private-installer will continue to accept unsigned artifacts in older versions; new installer releases prefer verification and will error by default unless the cluster has the corresponding public key configured. Documented key rotation and emergency bypass procedure in docs/RELEASE_PROCESS.md.

Related work: ENG-4532 (release hardening), ENG-4591 (installer verification UX).

review_comments: Ben Chu: Can we make the cosign public key an optional KMS URI or a raw PEM? Prefer KMS URI for hosted flow but allow PEM for air-gapped customers.
Asha Patel: Implemented both; CI supports KMS_URI and PEM_UPLOAD modes. Documented in RELEASE_PROCESS.md.
Priya Raman: Add a guard in the installer so verification failures provide actionable errors (which key to import, where to fetch SBOM).
Asha Patel: Added improved error messages and --no-verify flag for emergency rollbacks. See scripts/release/verify-release-artifacts.sh and installer consumer script.
Samir Kaur: CI linter flagged shellcheck warnings in generate-release-manifests.sh. Please address before merge.
Asha Patel: Fixed shellcheck issues and added a basic unit test for manifest schema validation.
notes: This PR centralizes release provenance for private-installer releases and is part of a larger effort to harden release controls for compliance-sensitive customers.

manual_steps: To perform an offline verification: download release-manifests.tgz, extract, run scripts/release/verify-release-artifacts.sh --manifest release-manifests.json --key /path/to/pubkey.pem
To rotate keys in production: follow docs/RELEASE_PROCESS.md -> Key Rotation section and re-run full release pipeline with new KMS URI.
